The error in the test `test_frame_series_axis` occurs at the line `result = op_func(other, axis=axis)`. The failure is due to an `AttributeError` when attempting to access the `value_counts` attribute on a numpy dtype object. This suggests that the code path where `op_func` equals `df.floordiv` or `df.divmod` (both of which are arithmetic operations that expect Series operands) is incorrectly handling the data types involved.

The test setup indicates that `other` should be either a column from the DataFrame (`self.frame.iloc[0, :]`) or another DataFrame column (`self.frame.iloc[:, 0]`). The error occurs when trying to perform an operation that expects a Series but receives a numpy dtype instead. This could happen if `other` is incorrectly interpreted as a single value rather than a column.

To fix this issue, the code should ensure that `other` is always treated as a pandas Series before performing arithmetic operations. Here are the methods where you can start fixing:

- `pandas.core.frame.DataFrame.floordiv`
- `pandas.core.frame.DataFrame.divmod`
- `pandas.core.series.Series.__floordiv__`
- `pandas.core.series.Series.__divmod__`

These methods should check if `other` is a numpy dtype and convert it to a pandas Series if necessary.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

pandas.core.frame.DataFrame.floordiv(other, axis='columns', level=None, fill_value=None)
pandas.core.frame.DataFrame.divmod(other, axis='columns', level=None, fill_value=None)
